description: OpenSSL Light for Windows (Shining Light Productions): the openssl command and its DLLs, without the development files. For keys, certificate requests and self-signed certificates, e.g. for the 3X-UI panel.
notes: Command: openssl. Scoop Apps: 'OpenSSL Light' shows the version and an example, then waits for a key.
Sets OPENSSL_CONF in your user environment to %USERPROFILE%\scoop\apps\OpenSSL-Light\current\bin\cnf\openssl.cnf;
open a new console after installing. 'scoop uninstall OpenSSL-Light' removes the variable again.
Self-signed certificate for a local panel (one line):
pre_install: # Every OpenSSL package in Scoop's main bucket adds the command 'openssl' and sets OPENSSL_CONF too.

if ($cmd -eq 'install' -and $others) { error "$app conflicts with $($others -join ', ') (Scoop's main bucket), installed: both add the command 'openssl' and set OPENSSL_CONF. Run 'scoop uninstall $($others -join ' ')' first. Scoop has already put $app into its app folder: run 'scoop uninstall $app' or simply install again, which cleans that up."; break }
# A copy from the slproweb installer can stay: it keeps its own folder and PATH entry, but reads OPENSSL_CONF too.

$outside = Get-ChildItem $roots -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-ItemProperty -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -like 'OpenSSL*' -and $_.Publisher -like 'OpenSSL Win* Installer Team' } | Select-Object -First 1

if ($cmd -eq 'install' -and $outside) { warn "$($outside.DisplayName) is also installed outside Scoop ($("$($outside.InstallLocation)" -replace [regex]::Escape($env:USERPROFILE), '%USERPROFILE%')). Both work side by side; the first one on PATH answers to 'openssl', and the OPENSSL_CONF this package sets applies to both." }

script: # openssl.exe without arguments waits for commands, so the shortcut opens this micro-launcher instead.
':: OpenSSL Light: shows the version and a few commands, then waits for a key.',
':: Written by the gesu Scoop bucket at install time.',
'ECHO OpenSSL Light for Windows (slproweb.com). Run it from any console as openssl.',
'ECHO Self-signed certificate for a local panel, valid for a year (one line):',
'ECHO Look at a certificate:     openssl x509 -in localhost.crt -noout -text',
'ECHO Check a site''s TLS:        openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com',
